core_obligations: Let F' be the Fourier-Mukai functor which is a sibling of F as in Lemma \reflemma-fully-faithful.

The case \dim(X) = 0. Here X is the spectrum of a finite (separable) extension k'/k and hence D_perf(\mathcalO_X) is equivalent to the category of graded k'-vector spaces such that \mathcalO_X corresponds to the trivial 1-dimensional vector
The case \dim(X) > 0. Here X is a projective smooth variety of dimension > 1.
proof_roadmap: 第 1 步：Let F' be the Fourier-Mukai functor which is a sibling of F as in Lemma \reflemma-fully-faithful.

第 2 步：The case \dim(X) = 0. Here X is the spectrum of a finite (separable) extension k'/k and hence D_perf(\mathcalO_X) is equivalent to the category of graded k'-vector spaces such that \mathcalO_X corresponds to the trivial 1-dimensional vector
第 3 步：The case \dim(X) > 0. Here X is a projective smooth variety of dimension > 1.
difficulty_reason: H2: Under exactly smooth proper X,Y over k and X projective, represent a k-linear exact fully faithful F by a perfect Fourier-Mukai kernel. Mandatory counted proof includes author equiv.tex2992-3259: resolve the diagonal by box products, apply F to the second factors, use negative-Ext vanishing to build compatible Postnikov systems, compare their transforms on zero-dimensional-support coherent sheaves, control moving cohomology windows and split off a stable perfect kernel K, then obtain a Fourier-Mukai sibling via the two-functor comparison. The final3278-3333 proof treats dimension zero separately and constructs enough negative objects by ample negative twists before applying sibling rigidity. Existing diagonal-resolution6034, bounded-fibre6026, cohomology-gap6055, two-functor6056 and sibling073 results may be cited; the new counted construction is the actual author kernel assembly and representability conclusion, not just the short final wrapper. All this core is explicitly in native proof_spans; the2pagePDF contains only the final theorem/proof.
